china_post_vaccination.population: general, HBsAg prevalence after universal infant vaccination (since 1992)

thresholds.HBsAg_positive: Indicates current HBV infection (acute or chronic)

clinical_features: Signs of chronic liver disease: spider angiomas, palmar erythema (advanced)
diagnosis.gold_standard: HBsAg positive for >6 months confirms chronic infection

treatment.indication: First-line oral antiviral for CHB; preferred in patients with potential pregnancy
First-line; preferred in patients with renal impairment or osteoporosis risk
First-line; preferred in treatment-naive patients without lamivudine resistance
Selected patients: HBeAg+, young, high ALT, low HBV DNA, no cirrhosis

treatment.method: HCC surveillance: ultrasound + AFP every 6 months
treatment.indication: All CHB patients, especially cirrhotics, males >40, family history of HCC

risk_factors: Perinatal transmission (mother-to-child — most common route in China)
prevention: Universal infant HBV vaccination (birth dose + 3-dose series)
HBV immunoglobulin (HBIG) for infants of HBsAg+ mothers
Antiviral prophylaxis during pregnancy (TDF) for high-viral-load mothers (HBV DNA >200,000 IU/mL)

clinical_examples.description: A 45-year-old man from Guangxi, born before universal HBV vaccination, found HBsAg+ on routine checkup. ALT 85 U/L, HBeAg+, HBV DNA 8.5×10^7 IU/mL. Liver FibroScan 6.8 kPa (F1). Mother also HBsAg+.
clinical_examples.key_findings: HBeAg+ chronic hepatitis B with active replication + mild ALT elevation + no significant fibrosis → treatment candidate
clinical_examples.outcome: Started tenofovir alafenamide 25mg daily. At 48 weeks: HBV DNA undetectable, ALT normalized, HBeAg seroconverted to anti-HBe. Continuing HCC surveillance every 6 months.
